question: When difference between compound and simple interest for three years is ₹152 at 4% interest per annum, the principal is ₹______
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for the difference between CI and SI for 3 years:

P = D × 100³ ÷ [R² × (300 + R)]

P = 152 × 1000000 ÷ [4² × (300 + 4)]

P = 152000000 ÷ [16 × 304]

P = 152000000 ÷ 4864 = 31250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹31250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference (D) = ₹152

Rate (R) = 4% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years:

D = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100)

 
 Simple Interest
 
 Diff = ₹152
 

 Total Compound Interest (3 Years)
 D = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 152 = P × (4/100)² × (3 + 4/100)

⇒ 152 = P × (1/25)² × (3 + 1/25)

⇒ 152 = P × (1/625) × (76/25)

⇒ 152 = P × (76 ÷ 15625)

⇒ P = (152 × 15625) ÷ 76

⇒ P = 2 × 15625

⇒ P = 31250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹31250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference for 2 years

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is calculated directly as: D = P × (R/100)²

Effective Rate for 2 years

The net effective compound interest rate for 2 years is: 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%

Effective Rate for 3 years

The net effective compound interest rate for 3 years is: 3R + (3R² ÷ 100) + (R³ ÷ 10000)%
